transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-16 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 mins
Attendees: Alice Park (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Nia Patel (Redwood CSM), Mark Caldwell (CTO), Leah Wong (Head of MLOps), Tom Rivera (Infra)
Links shared: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/caldwell-staging, https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/benchmark-profile (sample), security pack: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2-kms.pdf

[00:00] Alice Park: hey everyone thanks for carving time, appreciate it. quick check — sound and video ok?
[00:12] Mark Caldwell: yep, we can hear you, all good.
[00:18] Diego Ramos: awesome, i'll run through the technical runbook items and then we can sync on network and staging. i'm diego, se on the account.
[00:28] Leah Wong: great, i'm leah; i'm leading the ml ops side — main goal is get a pilot running behind our VPC with predictable p99 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:40] Alice Park: perfect. top-level agenda: 1) handoff of runbook and access, 2) confirm VPC/peering and encryption/KMS needs, 3) pilot scope & success criteria, 4) next steps and benchmark window.
[00:55] Tom Rivera: quick note — security team will insist on KMS integration and audit logs; also want SAML SSO for the console.
[01:05] Nia Patel: noted, we have an enterprise SSO playbook — we'll attach the SAML steps to the runbook we share.

[01:20] Diego Ramos: ok diving in — for the pilot we recommend starting with Redwood Hosted to validate prompts quickly, then flip to Dedicated or Private depending on throughput. timeline wise you said you wanted production within 6 weeks?
[01:35] Mark Caldwell: yes, 6–8 weeks ideally, but we can do a shorter pilot in 2 weeks if the infra is ready. main blocker is VPC peering with our cloud account.
[01:48] Leah Wong: also need to confirm data retention — we can't have user PII persisted outside our control. is there a purge or disable retention option?
[01:58] Alice Park: yes, we support no-retention profiles for enterprise and Private deployments. Diego can confirm the audit log retention and KMS flow.

[02:12] Diego Ramos: right — for Redwood Private we run customer-managed keys (HSM or KMS). for Hosted we can encrypt at rest and integrate with your KMS via an external key exchange, but audit trail sits in our control plane — we can push log forwarding to your SIEM via syslog.
[02:33] Leah Wong: syslog forwarding would be fine as long as we get immutable logs for at least 90 days.
[02:42] Diego Ramos: we can do that. there's a minor footnote: some older model variants don't support kv-cache checkpointing with external keys — you might see a slight hit on startup latencies for very long contexts.

[03:00] Mark Caldwell: can you unpack kv-cache and that startup concern?
[03:08] Diego Ramos: sure — kv cache is our prefix caching for in-flight tokens; if you have extremely long sequences, we keep long-term keys in memory. when using external KMS/HSM, we add a decryption step during instance initialisation which adds ~50–120 ms cold-start depending on instance type. normal steady-state token generation unaffected.
[03:34] Tom Rivera: hmm ok that matters for our p99 spikes. what about batching and autoscale? we want to avoid huge cost swings.
[03:45] Alice Park: that's where Redwood Optimize hooks help — Diego will propose batching thresholds and a policy to cap burst capacity. also you can pin to cheaper quantized variants for lower cost during non-critical windows.

[04:00] Diego Ramos: i'll sketch an autoscale policy: baseline Dedicated pool for predictable throughput during peak hours and a burst pool with fallback to a cheaper quantized model when capacity limited. that gives you an SLO for latency and a cost ceiling.
[04:15] Leah Wong: good. question — are we able to run some inference locally for half of the traffic to offload cost?
[04:23] Diego Ramos: you could do a hybrid route: local inference for deterministic tasks and Redwood for heavy LLM contexts. smart routing supports per-route policies by latency and model capability.

[04:40] [05:00] Speaker 1: sorry tiny crosstalk there.
[05:05] Alice Park: no worries. moving on to staging handoff — we need: 1) VPC peering info (CIDRs), 2) a service account with minimal privileges, 3) sample prompt sets, and 4) performance profile sheet. we shared a sample spreadsheet link in chat.
[05:24] Tom Rivera: i'll supply the CIDR and proxy requirements. we're behind a forward proxy for egress; is there an allowlist for that?
[05:33] Diego Ramos: yes allowlist IPs and TLS inspection caveats documented — if your proxy does TLS interception we need an exception for the TLS session, or you can use our private connector which establishes an outbound tunnel.
[05:46] Tom Rivera: outbound tunnel sounds better. can we do that in staging?
[05:51] Diego Ramos: yep, we'll include the connector steps in the runbook. small friction though: needs a thread to network to allow outbound to 3 endpoints: control plane, model runtime, and metrics sink.

[06:10] Leah Wong: on the model side — we currently run a tuned open Llama variant in-house. for quality we want parity checking between our baseline and the Redwood-curated variant. how do we measure quality regression?
[06:24] Nia Patel: we usually set up a prompt set of 300 golden prompts; Redwood Optimize can run nightly evals and alert if quality metrics drop beyond threshold. we'll link the eval harness.
[06:35] Diego Ramos: and we can snapshot model versions; if a new model variant regresses, the runbook supports automatic rollback to pinned versions.

[06:48] Mark Caldwell: ok good. I'd like to see the rollback behavior in action before we flip to Dedicated. can we schedule a canary deploy?
[06:56] Alice Park: yes canary is standard — we'll set up a 5% traffic canary with automatic rollback on latency or quality regressions. Diego will set the thresholds in the policy doc.

[07:10] [07:30] Speaker 2 (Tom): side question — cost estimate for 100 rps sustained with 1.2k prompt length?
[07:36] Diego Ramos: rough ballpark depends on model and quantization. for a quantized 8-bit variant in Dedicated you might see X tokens per GPU-hour — let me notate numbers after the call; we'll run an exact benchmark during scheduled window.
[07:49] Alice Park: we'll capture those cost permutations in the spreadsheet; Diego to run bench.

[08:05] Diego Ramos: technical deep dive note — if you need on-prem air-gapped, there's an on-prem package but it requires a longer lead time for certs and license. usually 8–12 weeks.
[08:19] Leah Wong: that's probably later stage. for now VPC Private deployment is the priority.

[08:30] Alice Park: quick walk through of the runbook sections (i'll call out file path): access checklist, network & peering, kms/integration, model pinning + rollout policy, observability hooks (traces/metrics), and incident playbook.
[08:45] Alice Park: the observability hooks will include token-level cost breakdown. do you need that exported to your billing system?
[08:52] Mark Caldwell: yes, finance wants a daily cost CSV with tags.
[08:58] Diego Ramos: we can push daily usage via S3 or forward to your billing API. we'll include tagging guidance.

[09:12] [09:40] Leah Wong: on SSO and RBAC — we want role separation: infra engineers, ml engineers, data reviewers. how granular is RBAC in the console?
[09:49] Nia Patel: roles are granular: admin, billing, deployer, observer, and a custom role you can create. SAML groups map to roles.
[09:58] Tom Rivera: perfect. please include example SAML attribute mappings.

[10:10] Diego Ramos: another note on caching — prefix cache for repeated prompts can reduce token generation by up to 30% for conversational workloads. for stateless batch tasks it's less effective.
[10:25] Leah Wong: most of our initial traffic is doc summarization, some multi-turn support, so caching may help.
[10:33] Diego Ramos: agreed; we'll enable prefix cache in staging and monitor hit rate.

[10:50] [11:15] Mark Caldwell: can you explain the difference in failure modes between Hosted and Dedicated? we want to understand fallback.
[11:24] Diego Ramos: Hosted has regional multi-tenant capacity with automatic routing; in rare cases of region saturation we failover to a sister region which can add 100–200 ms. Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs in a single region — more predictable latency but single-region risk; we provide a fallback policy to route to a compatible model in another region or to Hosted.
[11:48] Alice Park: we'll propose an HA strategy in the runbook: primary Dedicated pool + cross-region fallback to Hosted with a cost/latency tradeoff.

[12:05] Leah Wong: for compliance our SOC2 team asked whether we can surface per-request principal in audit logs.
[12:13] Diego Ramos: yes we can include request metadata: principal, route, model_version, and token_count. we'll add that to the audit schema doc.

[12:28] [12:50] Tom Rivera: anything about endpoint auth? we use mTLS internally. can we require mTLS for the private connector?
[12:58] Diego Ramos: yes the private connector supports mTLS. we recommend certificate rotation every 30 days; rotation steps are in the runbook.

[13:12] Alice Park: ok i want to capture timeline — propose: 1) network and access handed off in 2 business days, 2) staging deploy and smoke tests in week of 2026-06-22, 3) benchmark window during that week, 4) pilot canary run 5–10% traffic following benchmarks. does that align?
[13:33] Mark Caldwell: yes that maps.
[13:38] Leah Wong: we can commit to sample prompts and traffic profile by 2026-06-20.

[13:48] Diego Ramos: noted. on bench specifics: we'll run p95/p99 latency for your payloads, end-to-end time, GPU util, and token cost per 1k. also measure cold-start distribution.
[14:02] Alice Park: we'll record the bench results in the shared spreadsheet.

[14:10] [14:35] Speaker 3 (Mark): small ask — we want an SLA readout before Dedicated contract. do you have standard SLA targets?
[14:42] Nia Patel: yes enterprise Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and latency percentiles; i'll attach the SLA appendix to the runbook packet.
[14:52] Mark Caldwell: thanks.

[15:00] Diego Ramos: implementation risk checklist: network misconfiguration, proxy TLS interception, KMS latency on cold starts, and model regression. mitigation strategies listed in runbook section 7.
[15:18] Alice Park: we'll prioritize network and KMS items for the staging cutoff.

[15:28] [15:55] Leah Wong: question — are there guardrails for hallucinations or content filters?
[16:03] Diego Ramos: yes we have content filters and response schemas; you can enforce output validation and strip or block responses based on policy. Redwood also supports function-calling for structured outputs.
[16:18] Leah Wong: excellent. we'll need to test schema validation for our summarization outputs.

[16:30] Alice Park: last operations items: who is primary on your side for daily standups during the pilot?
[16:36] Leah Wong: that would be me, and Tom for infra. Mark will be on weekly check-ins.

[16:45] Alice Park: perfect. i'll summarize next steps in an email and upload the runbook.

[17:00] [17:20] Speaker 1: minor stutter.
[17:25] Mark Caldwell: no worries. anything else?
[17:30] Diego Ramos: one last note — we'll surface a cheap quantized model as option for background batch jobs; it reduces tokens/second cost noticeably.
[17:40] Leah Wong: yes that will help.

[17:50] Alice Park: recap — action items: we (Redwood) provide runbook, SAML mapping example, and staging connector steps; customer provides CIDR, proxy details, sample prompts, and traffic profile. Diego will prepare autoscale + bench plan. We'll set the bench window for week of 2026-06-22.
[18:15] Alice Park: i'll send calendar invites for the bench and a 30-min follow-up.

[18:25] Mark Caldwell: thanks everyone — feeling good about next steps.
[18:30] Leah Wong: thanks.
[18:33] Tom Rivera: thanks.
[18:35] Nia Patel: thanks team.

[18:40] Meeting end

Notes about transcript: automated speaker labels are imperfect in places; small disfluencies left in for fidelity.
